title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 10
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Annual passengers and sailings on five ferry routes:

Ardmore: 41,200 passengers, 620 sailings
Brindle: 128,400 passengers, 2,140 sailings
Carrick: 18,900 passengers, 210 sailings
Dunvarn: 76,500 passengers, 900 sailings
Eastport: 95,300 passengers, 1,270 sailings

Which route carries the most passengers per sailing?
options: A. Ardmore
B. Brindle
C. Dunvarn
D. Carrick
E. Eastport
questions.explanation: Passengers divided by sailings: Ardmore 66, Brindle 60, Carrick 90, Dunvarn 85, Eastport 75. Carrick is highest at about 90 a sailing, on the smallest route in the table. Brindle carries the most passengers overall but runs far more sailings to do it.

questions.prompt:
Cases on a waiting list at the end of each year:

2021: 20,000
2022: 15,000
2023: 14,200
2024: 13,900
2025: 9,600

In which year was the percentage fall from the previous year greatest?
options: E. The list rose in every year
questions.explanation: Year on year: 2022 -25.0%, 2023 -5.3%, 2024 -2.1%, 2025 -30.9%. 2025 is the largest fall at -30.9%. 2022 removed more cases in absolute terms (5,000) but from a much larger base.

questions.prompt:
Monthly sales (index, target 100) and returns as a percentage of orders (target: under 4%):

Jan: sales 112, returns 3.1%
Feb: sales 96, returns 2.8%
Mar: sales 105, returns 4.6%
Apr: sales 118, returns 3.9%
May: sales 88, returns 5.2%
Jun: sales 121, returns 2.2%
Jul: sales 103, returns 4.1%
Aug: sales 99, returns 3.4%

In how many months did the branch beat the sales target and stay under the returns target?
options: A. One
B. Two
C. Four
D. Five
E. Three
questions.explanation: 5 months beat the sales target: Jan, Mar, Apr, Jun, Jul. Of those, Mar (4.6%) and Jul (4.1%) missed the returns target, leaving 3: Jan, Apr, Jun.

questions.prompt:
Eight readings, in order: 40, 44, 47, 47, 49, 50, 51, 52

Which statement about these readings is accurate?
options: A. The mean is greater than the median
B. The median is greater than the mean and the mode is less than the median
C. The mode and the median are equal
D. The range is greater than the median
E. The mean and the mode are equal
questions.explanation: Mean 47.5, median 48, mode 47, range 12. The single low reading of 40 pulls the mean below the median, so median is greater than mean, while the repeated 47 sits below both. The range, 12, is far smaller than either average.

questions.prompt:
Alloy A is 30% copper and alloy B is 70% copper. They are to be blended into 40 kg of metal that is 45% copper.

Select the mass of alloy A required AND the mass of alloy B required.
options: A. 15 kg of A; 25 kg of B
B. 20 kg of A; 20 kg of B
C. 25 kg of A; 15 kg of B
D. 28 kg of A; 12 kg of B
E. The target cannot be reached with these two alloys
questions.explanation: The blend needs 18 kg of copper. With x kg of A: 0.30x + 0.70(40 - x) = 18, so 28 - 0.4x = 18 and x = 25. That leaves 15 kg of B. Equal masses would give 50% copper, above the target.

questions.prompt:
Units sold, this year against last:

Product P: 240 rising to 312
Product Q: 1,850 rising to 2,146

Select the product with the higher percentage growth AND the product with the higher growth in units.
options: A. Product P on both measures
B. Product Q on both measures
C. Product Q on percentage growth; Product P on growth in units
D. The two products grew equally on both measures
E. Product P on percentage growth; Product Q on growth in units
questions.explanation: Percentage growth: Product P 30.0%, Product Q 16.0%. Growth in units: Product P 72, Product Q 296. The smaller product grows faster in percentage terms while the larger one adds more units, so the two measures name different products.

questions.prompt:
Machine A alone completes a job in 10 hours and machine B alone in 15 hours. They start together and run until the job is done.

Select the time the job takes AND the machine that completes the larger share of it.
options: A. 6 hours; machine A does more of the job
B. 6 hours; machine B does more of the job
C. 12.5 hours; machine A does more of the job
D. 6 hours; the two do equal shares
E. 25 hours; machine A does more of the job
questions.explanation: Rates add: one tenth plus one fifteenth is one sixth of the job an hour, so the job takes 6 hours. In that time A does 6/10 = 60% of it and B the remaining 40%. Averaging the two times would give 12.5 hours, longer than A takes on its own.

questions.prompt:
GBP 5,000.00 is placed for 3 years. Account X pays 6% compounded annually; account Y pays 6% simple interest.

Select the account with the larger balance after 3 years AND the difference between the two balances.
options: A. Account Y; GBP 55.08
B. Account X; GBP 300.00
C. The two accounts are equal after three years
D. Account X; GBP 55.08
E. Account Y; GBP 900.00
questions.explanation: Compounding gives GBP 5,000.00 multiplied by 1.06 three times over: GBP 5,955.08. Simple interest gives GBP 5,000.00 plus GBP 900.00: GBP 5,900.00. Account X is ahead by GBP 55.08, because compounding pays interest on the interest already credited.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): funded posts — Trust A 4,200, Trust B 1,800, Trust C 6,500

SOURCE 2 (table): vacant posts — Trust A 315, Trust B 162, Trust C 429

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Recruitment support goes to the trust with the highest proportion of its posts vacant."

Which trust receives the support?
options: A. Trust A
B. Trust B
C. Trust C
D. The three trusts are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Vacancies as a share of funded posts: Trust A 7.5%, Trust B 9.0%, Trust C 6.6%. Trust B is highest and is also the smallest trust. Trust C has the most vacant posts in total, 429, but the largest establishment to spread them across.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "The recycling rate rose from 34% to 52% in a single year."

SOURCE 2 (note): "From April, garden waste collected separately has been counted as recycled. It was previously excluded."

SOURCE 3 (table): garden waste is 21% of all tonnage collected.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Households recycled 18 percentage points more material than before
B. The recycling rate would have fallen without the change
C. Much of the rise reflects a change in what counts as recycled rather than more recycling
D. Garden waste is the only material the authority recycles
E. The reclassification had no effect on the reported rate
questions.explanation: A category worth 21% of tonnage moved into the numerator part-way through the year, which on its own can account for most of the 18-point rise. The sources do not say the rate would have fallen without it, so the option claiming that goes further than the evidence carries.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): land under crop — Farm 1 340 hectares, Farm 2 150 hectares, Farm 3 420 hectares

SOURCE 2 (table): yield — Farm 1 8.2 tonnes per hectare, Farm 2 11.6 tonnes per hectare, Farm 3 6.9 tonnes per hectare

SOURCE 3 (email): "We need the single largest supply of grain, whatever the yield per hectare."

Which farm should the buyer approach?
options: A. Farm 1
B. Farm 2
C. All three produce the same tonnage
D. Cannot be determined from the sources
E. Farm 3
questions.explanation: Tonnage is area multiplied by yield: Farm 1 2,788 tonnes, Farm 2 1,740 tonnes, Farm 3 2,898 tonnes. Farm 3 is largest. Farm 2 farms the land hardest at 11.6 tonnes a hectare but has the least of it, so yield alone misreads the question.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Average class size fell from 24.5 to 22."

SOURCE 2 (table): classes ran from 28 to 34 over the same period.

SOURCE 3 (email): "Governors want to know what happened to the number of pupils on roll."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. The number of pupils rose by about 9%
B. The number of pupils fell
C. The number of pupils was unchanged
D. The number of pupils cannot be calculated from these sources
E. Teaching quality improved
questions.explanation: Pupils on roll are classes multiplied by average class size: before, 28 multiplied by 24.5 is 686; after, 34 multiplied by 22 is 748 — a rise of about 9%. Source 1 alone points the other way, which is why the count of classes decides it.

questions.prompt:
What is the area of a rectangular plot?

(1) The perimeter of the plot is 68 metres.
(2) The plot is 4 metres longer than it is wide.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), length plus width is 34, which fits 17 by 17, 20 by 14 and many other areas. (2) fixes the shape but not the size. Together, w plus (w + 4) is 34, so w is 15 and the length is 19, giving an area of 285 square metres. Neither statement alone reaches a single value.

questions.prompt:
Is the positive integer n divisible by 6?

(1) n is divisible by 12.
(2) n is divisible by 3.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Every multiple of 12 is a multiple of 6, so (1) answers the question with a definite yes. (2) admits both 3, which is not divisible by 6, and 6, which is, so it settles nothing on its own. The two are consistent, since 12 is also a multiple of 3.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of x?

(1) 3x - 7 = 20
(2) x squared is 81 and x is positive.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), 3x is 27 and x is 9. From (2), x is 9 or -9, and the positivity condition leaves 9. Each statement alone fixes the same value, so either is sufficient by itself.

questions.prompt:
By what percentage did a company's revenue change from 2023 to 2024?

(1) Revenue rose by GBP 240,000.
(2) Revenue in 2024 was 1.15 times revenue in 2023.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives the size of the rise but not what it is a rise from: on GBP 1 million that is 24%, on GBP 4 million it is 6%. (2) is the ratio itself, so the change is 15% whatever the base. Together they would also fix the base at GBP 1.6 million, but the question asks only for the percentage.

questions.prompt:
Which depot covers the most miles per vehicle?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 journeys | Annual mileage | Punctuality
Ashbury | 42 | 2.9 | 1,180,000 | 81%
Bramfield | 78 | 1.6 | 2,340,000 | 94%
Cranleigh | 25 | 4.7 | 610,000 | 79%
Denholme | 61 | 3.4 | 1,400,000 | 83%
Eastgate | 94 | 1.1 | 2,162,000 | 96%
Foxton | 37 | 5.2 | 740,000 | 74%
options: A. Ashbury
B. Denholme
C. Eastgate
D. Foxton
E. Bramfield
questions.explanation: Mileage divided by vehicles: Ashbury 28,095, Bramfield 30,000, Cranleigh 24,400, Denholme 22,951, Eastgate 23,000, Foxton 20,000. Bramfield is highest at 30,000 miles a vehicle. Bramfield covers more miles in total but runs the largest fleet to do it.

questions.prompt:
How many depots record punctuality below the median for the six?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 journeys | Annual mileage | Punctuality
Ashbury | 42 | 2.9 | 1,180,000 | 81%
Bramfield | 78 | 1.6 | 2,340,000 | 94%
Cranleigh | 25 | 4.7 | 610,000 | 79%
Denholme | 61 | 3.4 | 1,400,000 | 83%
Eastgate | 94 | 1.1 | 2,162,000 | 96%
Foxton | 37 | 5.2 | 740,000 | 74%
options: A. One
B. Three
C. Two
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: Punctuality in order: 74, 79, 81, 83, 94, 96. With six values the median is the average of the third and fourth, so (81 + 83) / 2 = 82. Below it: Ashbury 81%, Cranleigh 79%, Foxton 74% — 3 depots.

questions.prompt:
Taking the average journey as 10 miles, which depot suffers the most breakdowns in a year?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 journeys | Annual mileage | Punctuality
Ashbury | 42 | 2.9 | 1,180,000 | 81%
Bramfield | 78 | 1.6 | 2,340,000 | 94%
Cranleigh | 25 | 4.7 | 610,000 | 79%
Denholme | 61 | 3.4 | 1,400,000 | 83%
Eastgate | 94 | 1.1 | 2,162,000 | 96%
Foxton | 37 | 5.2 | 740,000 | 74%
options: A. Ashbury
B. Bramfield
C. Cranleigh
D. Denholme
E. Foxton
questions.explanation: Journeys are mileage divided by 10, and breakdowns are journeys divided by 100 multiplied by the rate: Ashbury 3,422, Bramfield 3,744, Cranleigh 2,867, Denholme 4,760, Eastgate 2,378, Foxton 3,848. Denholme is highest. Foxton has much the worst rate, 5.2 per 100 journeys, but covers too few miles for it to add up.

questions.prompt:
Which depot is above the six-depot average on both miles per vehicle and punctuality?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 journeys | Annual mileage | Punctuality
Ashbury | 42 | 2.9 | 1,180,000 | 81%
Bramfield | 78 | 1.6 | 2,340,000 | 94%
Cranleigh | 25 | 4.7 | 610,000 | 79%
Denholme | 61 | 3.4 | 1,400,000 | 83%
Eastgate | 94 | 1.1 | 2,162,000 | 96%
Foxton | 37 | 5.2 | 740,000 | 74%
options: A. Ashbury
B. Cranleigh
C. Bramfield
D. Eastgate
E. Foxton
questions.explanation: The average is 24,741 miles a vehicle and 84.5% punctuality. Above on mileage per vehicle: Ashbury, Bramfield. Above on punctuality: Bramfield, Eastgate. Bramfield is the only depot on both lists.
